title: Writing outside the constrained indices
statement: Let $K$ be a predicate on the natural numbers and let $\mu,\mu'$ be integer-valued sequences. If they agree wherever $K$ holds, and $K$ does not hold at an index $b$, then for every integer $x$, replacing the value of $\mu'$ at $b$ by $x$ leaves it agreeing with $\mu$ wherever $K$ holds.
